Native R provenance-preserving trajectories and versioned snapshots

etr_native_trajectory_provenance.Rd

Python-independent handling of TrajectorySet-like scientific provenance, nonmutating transformations and native R snapshot restore. The source of the with_values semantics is the published Python eyetrajectoriespy 1.2.0 types.py definition. Native R snapshots are not Python portable-scientific-result JSON and NPZ bundles.

Usage

etr_trajectory_provenance(x)

etr_with_values(x, values = x$values, time = NULL,
                provenance_update = NULL, time_unit = NULL,
                coordinate_system = NULL)

etr_trajectory_snapshot(x)

etr_restore_trajectory_snapshot(snapshot)

Arguments

x

A native R etr_trajectory_set, including objects created before the provenance field was added.

values

A numeric three-dimensional trajectory array with compatible curve/time/channel shape. Explicit R NA_real_ means missing gaze.

time

Optional strictly increasing finite time vector. NULL retains the original grid.

provenance_update

Optional JSON-like named R list with unique, nonempty keys. Updated top-level keys replace existing entries; unlike utils::modifyList, nested dictionaries are not recursively merged.

time_unit,coordinate_system

Optional single nonempty character scalars; NULL retains the corresponding existing unit.

snapshot

A version-one etr_trajectory_snapshot list. Only use untrusted serialized files after separate input-security review.

Value

etr_trajectory_provenance() returns an independent JSON-like named list, with an empty list for legacy native trajectory objects.

etr_with_values() returns a new native R trajectory collection without modifying x; existing curve IDs, channel names and one-row-per-curve metadata are retained.

etr_trajectory_snapshot() returns an etr_trajectory_snapshot S3 list with the exact R numeric array, time vector, IDs, metadata and factors, coordinate/time units, provenance, format label, schema version and array shape. Snapshots record an explicit Python boundary mode when the original trajectory uses it.

etr_restore_trajectory_snapshot() validates the snapshot and reconstructs a native etr_trajectory_set.

Details

The etr_trajectory_set() constructor now accepts optional provenance=list() as the last formal argument, preserving every older positional argument. etr_validate() checks provenance, etr_subset() retains it and etr_from_long() appends source audit defaults. Stage 3 normalization/centering operations preserve earlier provenance and append documented Python preprocessing keys.

Python's TrajectorySet is a frozen dataclass, whose with_values() method uses a shallow top-level dictionary update. This R-native implementation follows those audit semantics without reticulate. For some unrelated older native R transforms, provenance retention is not yet fully implemented or verified.

A native snapshot can be saved with saveRDS() and read back with readRDS(); it is meant for trusted native R environments. It is NOT the cross-language, audited eyetrajectoriespy export_portable_result() scientific-result schema, which stores JSON and NPZ and has different manifest/array hash requirements. Do not imply compatible Python loading, cryptographic verification, execution sandboxing, or full public API parity.

Examples

time <- c(0,.2,1,2)
values <- array(1:16,c(2,4,2))
x <- etr_trajectory_set(time,values,curve_ids=c("A","B"),
                        dimension_names=c("x","y"),
                        provenance=list(source="recording"))
y <- etr_with_values(x,values=values+1,
                     provenance_update=list(preprocessing="offset"))
stopifnot(identical(y$provenance$source,"recording"))
snapshot <- etr_trajectory_snapshot(y)
restored <- etr_restore_trajectory_snapshot(snapshot)
stopifnot(identical(restored,y))
